clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old male with a history of alcoholism and heavy smoking presented with chronic (3 years) itchy hyperpigmented patches on his right trunk and right thigh. Initial workup included blood tests, which were normal except for a slight increase in white blood cell count, and a chest and abdomen CT scan, which was normal. A skin biopsy revealed parakeratosic hyperkeratosic epidermis with slight spongiosis, moderate infiltration of the papillary dermis by atypical lymphocytes with mild deposition of melanophages, and lymphocytic infiltrate in clusters and in linear basilar distribution along the dermoepidermal junction. Immunohistochemistry showed these atypical lymphocytes were CD3+, CD8+, CD4−, and CD20−. The known final diagnosis is early stage Hypopigmented Mycosis Fungoides (HPMF).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with chronic itchy hyperpigmented patches on the right trunk and right thigh for 3 years.

Histopathological examination of skin biopsy revealed parakeratosic hyperkeratosic epidermis with slight spongiosis, moderate infiltration of papillary dermis by atypical lymphocytes with mild deposition of melanophages, and lymphocytic infiltrate in clusters and in linear basilar distribution along the dermoepidermal junction.
Immunohistochemistry of atypical lymphocytes showed a CD3+, CD8+, CD4−, CD20− phenotype.
Systemic workup, including blood tests (except for slight WBC elevation) and chest/abdomen CT scan, was largely normal, indicating no systemic involvement.
